correctness.rationale: All canonical configurations are explicit. Direct graph-Laplacian linearization gives A=1+2r+3s, B=-1+2r-3s, C=-1/2-r+3s, and exact transverse eigenvalues. Necessary and sufficient strict inequalities yield the sharp wedge. The sine interaction is odd, producing a genuine gradient flow. A positive quadratic-plus-quartic potential at B=0 proves the nonhyperbolic pacemaker attractor; u′=-g(5r-4)u^3+O(u^5) gives the exact t u(t)^2 limit. The splay lower boundary has a sign-changing cubic potential and is not attracting. The implicit-function theorem proves robust continuation and delay derivative. Independent SymPy algebraic checks run from the included script. No extrapolation from finite experiments to infinite time.

value.rationale: The 2026 three-cell inhibitory phase reduction exhibits multiple neuronal rhythm types numerically. A sharp natural third-harmonic parameter region in which all six canonical rhythms coexist, its one-sided attracting critical face, and the exact critical relaxation coefficient supply a nontrivial constructive and quantitative answer to how multirhythmic coexistence and loss of exponential stability occur in the simplest symmetric phase triad. The strict versus algebraic distinction is relevant to finite-time numerical classification near a pitchfork edge. This is a narrow exact phase-model result, not a claim about actual delayed neuronal dynamics.
